DS-Albireo.title: Albireo · telescope photograph
DS-Albireo.note: A telescope exposure shows the two colored components. This is not a handheld binocular simulation. The source image is displayed without editing.

DS-MizarAlcor.title: Mizar & Alcor · telescope photograph
DS-MizarAlcor.credit: Thomas Bresson; source scaled by Antonsusi · Wikimedia Commons
DS-MizarAlcor.note: The telescope photograph resolves Mizar’s close binary as well as the wide Alcor companion. Ordinary binoculars reveal the wide pair. StarHop displays the source image without further editing.
DS-MizarAlcor.shortCredit: Thomas Bresson; source scaled by Antonsusi

STAR-Betelgeuse.title: Betelgeuse · ALMA stellar disk
STAR-Betelgeuse.credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO) / E. O’Gorman / P. Kervella · Wikimedia Commons
STAR-Betelgeuse.note: A false-color submillimeter image resolves the star’s disk. Binoculars show a point of light; they cannot resolve this surface. The source image is displayed without editing.

STAR-Sirius.title: Sirius · optical photograph
STAR-Sirius.note: A real optical photograph shows Sirius as a bright point against its star field. The photographic diffraction spikes are not the star’s physical shape; Sirius B is not resolved here.

STAR-Vega.title: Vega · optical telescope photograph
STAR-Vega.note: A real optical exposure of Vega and its surrounding stars. The star remains a point in binoculars; the photographic halo is not its physical diameter.

M27.title: Dumbbell Nebula · ESO optical composite
M27.credit: ESO / I. Appenzeller, W. Seifert, O. Stahl, M. Zamani
M27.note: An optical broadband and emission-line composite resolves the nebula. Binoculars show a much smaller, fainter patch without these colors.

M7.title: Ptolemy Cluster · ESO optical photograph
M7.note: Wide Field Imager optical photograph of the open cluster. Binoculars reveal its brighter members; the deep background is a long-exposure effect.

M13.title: Hercules Globular Cluster · optical photograph
M13.note: A resolved telescope view of the cluster. Ordinary binoculars show a compact unresolved glow.

M43.title: M43 · optical telescope photograph
M43.note: A monochrome optical view isolates M43 above the much brighter Orion Nebula. Binoculars reveal less nebulous detail.

M62.title: M62 · Hubble optical close-up
M62.credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, S. Anderson et al.
M62.note: A Hubble close-up of this asymmetric globular cluster. The resolved stars are a telescope view, not a binocular simulation.

M108.title: Surfboard Galaxy · optical telescope photograph
M108.note: A long-exposure optical photograph shows the edge-on galaxy without the trail crossing the historical survey plate. Original photographer annotations are retained.

M64.title: Black Eye Galaxy · Hubble optical composite
M64.credit: NASA and the Hubble Heritage Team (AURA/STScI)
M64.note: Hubble resolves the dark dust lane and bright nucleus. Binoculars do not reveal this level of detail.
M64.shortCredit: NASA and the Hubble Heritage Team (AURA/STScI)

M97.title: Owl Nebula · optical telescope photograph
M97.note: An optical telescope exposure shows the nebula without the trail crossing the old survey plate. Its eye-like detail is not a binocular expectation.

NGC6530.title: NGC 6530 in the Lagoon Nebula · optical photograph
NGC6530.note: NGC 6530 is the group of blue stars to the left of the bright Lagoon Nebula core in this wider optical exposure. Binoculars show the cluster more readily than faint nebulosity.

M8.title: Lagoon Nebula and NGC 6530 · ESO optical photograph
M8.note: NGC 6530 is the group of blue stars to the left of the bright Lagoon Nebula core in this wider optical exposure. Binoculars show the cluster more readily than faint nebulosity.

M16.title: Eagle Nebula and its cluster · ESO optical mosaic
M16.note: An optical B/V/R mosaic shows the star cluster and Eagle Nebula. Binoculars reveal the cluster much more readily than the pillars and gas.

M20.title: Trifid Nebula · ESO optical photograph
M20.note: A deep optical exposure shows the emission and reflection nebulae and dark dust lanes. Binoculars show much less detail and color.

M42.title: Orion Nebula · Hubble optical mosaic
M42.credit: NASA, ESA, M. Robberto (STScI/ESA) and the Hubble Space Telescope Orion Treasury Project Team
M42.note: An optical mosaic combines exposures to retain bright and faint structure. It is a telescope reference, not a simulated binocular view.

NGC3372.title: Carina Nebula · ESO optical mosaic
NGC3372.note: A deep optical mosaic shows the nebula and its bright star fields without the flat clipped areas of the historical survey display.

M17.title: Omega Nebula · VST optical photograph
M17.credit: ESO / INAF-VST / OmegaCAM; acknowledgement: OmegaCen / Astro-WISE / Kapteyn Institute
M17.note: A wide optical telescope exposure shows the Omega Nebula and its surrounding field. The small bright patch is the binocular goal; these colors and fine gas structures are photographic detail.
